issues.title: support enableQuotedIdentifier: false in the MSSQL dialect.
issues.body:
Hey 👋

Setting tedious's `options.enableQuotedIdentifier` to `false` sends `SET QUOTED_IDENTIFIER OFF`, but our MSSQL compiler still uses double quotes for identifiers.

For example, on `kysely@0.29.7`:

```ts
db.selectFrom('person').select('name').compile().sql
// select "name" from "person"
```

With `QUOTED_IDENTIFIER OFF`, double quotes delimit string literals instead of identifiers, so this SQL is incompatible with the connection setting.

Could we use SQL Server's `[name]` syntax in `MssqlQueryCompiler` instead?

```sql
select [name] from [person]
```

Bracketed identifiers work with both `QUOTED_IDENTIFIER ON` and `OFF`, so we wouldn't need to inspect the connection option or generate different SQL for each setting.

We'd also need bracket-specific escaping: `a]b` becomes `[a]]b]`, while `[` inside an identifier stays unchanged. Simply changing the wrappers isn't enough, since our shared `sanitizeIdentifier` currently doubles both opening and closing delimiters.

Relevant source: [our MSSQL compiler](https://github.com/kysely-org/kysely/blob/ac876c212cfec0e62a77cccc39c7417a13d11ab0/src/dialect/mssql/mssql-query-compiler.ts), [identifier escaping](https://github.com/kysely-org/kysely/blob/ac876c212cfec0e62a77cccc39c7417a13d11ab0/src/query-compiler/default-query-compiler.ts#L1863-L1882).

Microsoft documents that [bracketed identifiers are unaffected by QUOTED_IDENTIFIER](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/t-sql/statements/set-quoted-identifier-transact-sql) and shows the [closing-bracket escaping rules](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/t-sql/functions/quotename-transact-sql).

issues.title: reject mysql2's nestTables and rowsAsArray options.
issues.body:
Hey 👋

mysql2's pool-level `nestTables` and `rowsAsArray` options change the shape of query results. We currently accept them without validation, while still typing the results as flat objects. 😬

Repro (`kysely@0.29.7`, `mysql2@3.24.6`):

```ts
import { Kysely, MysqlDialect, sql } from 'kysely'
import mysql from 'mysql2'

const pool = mysql.createPool({
  uri: process.env.DATABASE_URL!,
  nestTables: true,
})
const db = new Kysely({ dialect: new MysqlDialect({ pool }) })

try {
  const { rows } = await sql<{ id: number }>`
    select t.id from (select 42 as id) as t
  `.execute(db)

  console.log(rows) // [{ t: { id: 42 } }]
  console.log(rows[0]!.id) // undefined, typed as number
} finally {
  await db.destroy()
}
```

Verified the same query with each configuration:

| Pool option | Actual `rows` |
| --- | --- |
| Defaults | `[{ id: 42 }]` |
| `nestTables: true` | `[{ t: { id: 42 } }]` |
| `nestTables: '_'` | `[{ t_id: 42 }]` |
| `nestTables: ''` | `[{ tid: 42 }]` |
| `rowsAsArray: true` | `[[42]]` |

We should reject these configurations in `MysqlDialect` with a clear error before executing queries.

A truthiness check for `nestTables` isn't enough. mysql2 treats every string, including `''`, as an active mode, so the check should cover `nestTables === true || typeof nestTables === 'string'`, alongside `rowsAsArray: true`.

If validation happens after acquiring a connection, we should release it before throwing.

Relevant source: [mysql2's row parser](https://github.com/sidorares/node-mysql2/blob/v3.24.6/lib/parsers/text_parser.js), [our MySQL driver](https://github.com/kysely-org/kysely/blob/ac876c212cfec0e62a77cccc39c7417a13d11ab0/src/dialect/mysql/mysql-driver.ts).
issues.author: igalklebanov

issues.title: support or reject enableImplicitTransactions: true in the MSSQL dialect.
issues.body:
Hey 👋

tedious exposes `options.enableImplicitTransactions: true`, which sends `SET IMPLICIT_TRANSACTIONS ON` when connecting.

In this mode, ordinary statements like `INSERT` or `UPDATE` can start a transaction without an explicit `db.transaction()` call. Completing the statement doesn't commit that transaction.

Our normal query path acquires a connection, executes the request, and releases the connection back to the pool. We don't commit or roll back an implicit transaction, and `resetConnectionsOnRelease` defaults to `false`.

Based on that release path, a single-connection pool can end up doing this:

1. An ordinary query starts an implicit transaction.
2. We release the connection with that transaction still open.
3. An unrelated query borrows the same connection and runs in the existing transaction.
4. A later commit or rollback affects work from earlier borrowers too. 😬

This can leave writes uncommitted and locks held after a query finishes. It also means the transaction state doesn't match the boundaries Kysely manages.

We should either find a way to support this mode safely across ordinary queries and our transaction APIs, or detect it and throw a clear error.

If inspecting the underlying tedious configuration isn't reliable, `SELECT @@OPTIONS & 2 AS implicit_transactions` can detect whether the session currently has implicit transactions enabled.

Resetting on release alone wouldn't define the intended commit behavior for ordinary writes, so we should account for that if we go down the support route.

Found during source review of `kysely@0.29.7` / `tedious@20.3.7`: [normal connection lifecycle](https://github.com/kysely-org/kysely/blob/ac876c212cfec0e62a77cccc39c7417a13d11ab0/src/driver/default-connection-provider.ts), [MSSQL release path](https://github.com/kysely-org/kysely/blob/ac876c212cfec0e62a77cccc39c7417a13d11ab0/src/dialect/mssql/mssql-driver.ts#L103-L109), [reset option and its default](https://github.com/kysely-org/kysely/blob/ac876c212cfec0e62a77cccc39c7417a13d11ab0/src/dialect/mssql/mssql-dialect-config.ts#L1-L8).

See also [tedious's connection option](https://tediousjs.github.io/tedious/api-connection.html) and [SQL Server's implicit transaction behavior and detection](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/t-sql/statements/set-implicit-transactions-transact-sql).
issues.author: igalklebanov

issues.title: don't return busy connections to the pool after driver-side query timeouts.
issues.body:
Hey 👋

`pg`'s `query_timeout` is a client-side timeout. It rejects the query call without cancelling the query on the database side.

When that happens, we consider the query finished and return the connection to the pool, even though PostgreSQL may still be running it. The next caller can acquire that client, queue behind the first query, and time out without its query ever reaching the server. 😬

Repro (`kysely@0.29.7`, `pg@8.23.1`):

```js
import { Kysely, PostgresDialect, sql } from 'kysely'
import pg from 'pg'

const pool = new pg.Pool({
  connectionString: process.env.DATABASE_URL,
  max: 1,
  query_timeout: 1000,
})
const db = new Kysely({ dialect: new PostgresDialect({ pool }) })

await sql`select pg_sleep(3)`
  .execute(db)
  .catch((error) => console.log('first query:', error.message))

console.log('idle clients:', pool.idleCount)

await sql`select 1`
  .execute(db)
  .catch((error) => console.log('next query:', error.message))

await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 1500))
console.log('after sleep:', (await sql`select 1 as one`.execute(db)).rows)

await db.destroy()
```

```text
first query: Query read timeout
idle clients: 1
next query: Query read timeout
after sleep: [ { one: 1 } ]
```

Reproduced 3/3 runs on PostgreSQL 18.3 and Node 26.7.0. An independent connection checked `pg_stat_activity` after both timeouts: the backend was still `active`, waiting on `PgSleep`, and executing the first query. The final query reused that same backend.

We [release the connection in `finally`](https://github.com/kysely-org/kysely/blob/ac876c212cfec0e62a77cccc39c7417a13d11ab0/src/driver/default-connection-provider.ts#L20-L24), and the PostgreSQL connection's [release method calls plain `client.release()`](https://github.com/kysely-org/kysely/blob/ac876c212cfec0e62a77cccc39c7417a13d11ab0/src/dialect/postgres/postgres-driver.ts#L284-L286).

Passing an `AbortSignal` doesn't protect against the driver's timeout winning first. We take the [ordinary query error/release path](https://github.com/kysely-org/kysely/blob/ac876c212cfec0e62a77cccc39c7417a13d11ab0/src/query-executor/query-executor-base.ts#L132-L140).

We need to stop assuming that `DatabaseConnection.executeQuery()` settling means the connection is ready to be reused. The connection lifecycle handling should be shared, with drivers identifying failures that leave execution state uncertain. Ordinary SQL errors should still allow reuse when the connection is healthy.
